description: A wide two-dimensional performance pad: dragging across it puts out a note voltage from the horizontal position and a level from the vertical one, with a modulation input that can be routed to either.

params.text: Sets the octave the left edge of the pad starts at, -5 to +4.
Sets how many octaves the pad covers, 1 to 5.
Chooses the shape mapping the vertical position to the level: straight, two eased curves, a sine, and a step that jumps to full as soon as the pad is touched.
Quantises the note output to the guide the menu is set to, instead of sliding smoothly across the pad.
Sets how much of the modulation is added to the note output, -1 to +1, at half a semitone per unit.
Sets how much of the modulation is added to the level output, -1 to +1; it only has an effect while the pad is being dragged.
Passes the modulation going to the note output through the curve as well, scaled by where the finger is vertically.
Passes the modulation going to the level output through the curve as well.
Applies the level modulation to the VCA output too, multiplying the gain by it.
Tells the module what span the modulation voltage covers so it can be scaled to plus or minus one: -5V to +5V, 0V to +10V or 0V to +5V.

inputs.text: An external signal for the pad to act as a VCA on, polyphonic.
The modulation source; a polyphonic cable uses its first channel for the note routing and its second for the level routing.

outputs.text: The note from the horizontal position at 1V per octave plus any note modulation, clamped to ±10V.
The level from the vertical position with the curve applied, 0V to 10V unless the menu says otherwise.
10V while the pad is being dragged and 0V when it is let go.
The external input passed through the pad's vertical position as a VCA, clamped to ±5V, with the same number of channels; it is silent while the pad is not being dragged.
Five channels: the note, the level with the curve applied, the gate, the raw horizontal position at 0V to 10V and the raw vertical position.

notes: Nothing comes out until you drag on the pad with the mouse. The gate is high only while the button is held down.
The pad is the instrument: the bars drawn across it are note guides, and the left-to-right position sets the pitch while the up-and-down position sets the level.
The modulation routings do nothing without a cable in MOD IN, and the level routing does nothing unless the pad is being dragged.
menu: Show Guides — draws the note guide bars on the pad; turning it off leaves a plain surface.
Guide Type...: Semitones, Quartertones, Octaves — sets what the guide bars mark out, and with snapping on, what the note output snaps to.
Y-Axis Range (Non-VCA): 0V to 10V (Default), 0V to 5V, -5V to 5V — sets the span of the volume output; it does not change the VCA output.
Show Modulation While Playing — draws where the modulation is moving the note and the level while the pad is dragged.

outputs.0: 1V per octave · continuous · one channel only
